questions: Should the replacement be applied to the entire text as a whole (global substitution) or to each word in mystrings individually before splitting? The clarification mentions using re.sub on the entire text for each word, but does it imply overlapping replacements (e.g., if one word is a substring of another) should be handled sequentially, and if so, in what order?
What constitutes a 'word' for splitting the text after replacement? The reference uses text.split() which splits on whitespace, but should punctuation be considered part of words or separate tokens?

Are the words in mystrings expected to be matched as whole words only, or as substrings anywhere in the text? The reference uses re.sub without word boundaries, so it replaces substrings, but is that intended?

After replacement, should the frequency plot include words with zero frequency? The prompt says 'each unique word on the x-axis' but only after modification; if a word in mystrings doesn't appear, it wouldn't be in the text, so likely not, but is that explicit?

Should the order of words on the x-axis be based on first appearance in the modified text, or alphabetical, or something else? The prompt says 'in the order they appear after modification', but does 'appear' mean first occurrence in the text sequence?

Is the replacement case-insensitive for both matching and replacement? The clarification says 'uses re.sub on the entire text for each word in mystrings' with flags=re.IGNORECASE, but does the replaced text retain original case or become lowercase/uppercase?

What should happen if a word in mystrings contains spaces and underscores? Should underscores be added only to spaces, or also to existing underscores? The prompt says 'replace spaces with underscores', but not about handling underscores in input.
If mystrings contains duplicate entries, should they be processed multiple times? The reference loops over mystrings as given, so duplicates would cause repeated substitutions, but is that intended?
